title: Movies Under the Stars: Halloweentown
description: Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! This summer, NYC Parks and The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs.A benevolent witch must save her peaceful home town from an invading dark force.Rated TV-GContent suitable for all ages, with no material considered inappropriate for children.Movies begin at dusk. title: Proximity Exhibition
description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.
location: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)

title: The Garden
description: Flying Leap Productions, in association with the New 42 and the New Victory Theater present: The Garden The Garden is a radically inclusive outdoor performance that connects families with young children aged 0-5 living to parks and cultural institutions.  When: Sunday, October 4, 2026Session 1: 10:00 AM- 10:45 AMSession 2: 11:30 AM- 12:15 PMWhere: Shade Garden (located behind the Children’s Museum) (View Directions and Site Map)**In case of inclement weather, performances will take place in The Carpenter’s Shop**Admission: FREE | Please reserve one ticket for each family member  In The Garden, families experience the life cycle through all five senses – through movement theater, poetic text in multiple languages, and interactive play – seated in the grass beneath the open sky in their local public park, lawn, or greenspace.  Children and their families will connect to nature and to each other, building confidence and strengthening core synapses vital for child development. The Garden is New York City’s first and only show of its kind to provide the distinct benefits of theater by meeting audience members exactly where they are.  This performance is presented with support from the Snug Harbor Cultural Center and Botanical Garden and the Staten Island Children’s Museum.Developed as part of New Victory LabWorks Launch, powered by New 42, which receives support for baby and toddler work from Vienn and Salman Al-Rashid.The Garden is made possible by the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of the Office of the Governor and the New York State Legislature.
categories: Education | Best for Kids

title: Woodlawn Wednesdays: Forest Restoration and Invasive Removal
description: Hands-on forest restoration in the Northeast Forest at Woodlawn. We remove the invasive plants crowding out the young native trees regenerating here, and protect what is already coming back. Tools, gloves and guidance provided - no experience needed. Meet at Woodlawn Playground; we walk in together.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from September 2nd - September 30th. Dates are 9/2, 9/9, 9/16, 9/23, and 9/30.Space is limited to 30 volunteers each week. Groups of 6 or more should email noel@vancortlandt.org. Ages 15+ welcome; minors need a waiver.Register for a session

title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen
categories: Education | Nature | Art

title: Team RIVER Volunteers
description: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

title: Public Gallery Tour
description: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. Visitors can expect an in-depth look at artworks on view in Glyndor Gallery and in the Sunroom Project Space, showcasing the work of both emerging and established artists in the unique context of a public garden.  Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes. Registration is not required for this drop-in event. Today’s tour features current exhibitions. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.    Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant.

title: Spotlight tour: Horticulture
description: Dig deep into the High Line’s horticulture with a garden-focused tour! Each led by a knowledgeable High Line Docent, these 90-minute specialized tours offer an immersive look into the High Line’s rich and distinctive horticulture. Participants will gain a deep understanding of legendary garden designer Piet Oudolf’s naturalistic approach to plant selection, how the park’s over 500 species of plants contribute to the thriving ecosystems on the High Line and New York City, and much more.Horticulture tours will be led by docent Barbara Rohdie on September 3 and October 1.

title: Movies Under the Stars: Golden Door
description: Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! This summer, NYC Parks and The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs.Imaginative and enthralling romantic drama about a rustic Sicilian widower (Vincenzo Amato) who gets involved with a mysterious, aristocratic Englishwoman (Charlotte Gainsbourg) on an immigrant ship en route to America in 1904. The film title refers to the metaphoric passage made by passengers through Ellis Island and into the New World. Written and directed by Emanuele Crialese. Also known as "Nuovomondo."Rated PG-13: Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13. Parents are urged to be cautious.Movies begin at dusk. This event is FREE and open to the public. Glass bottles and alcoholic beverages are strictly prohibited. In the event of heavy rain or extreme weather, the screening may be canceled. The decision to cancel the event will be made prior to the screening and will be promptly posted on our website.For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call 311. Contact (212) 360-1430 or accessibility@parks.nyc.gov for more information regarding accessibility.

title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

title: Proximity Exhibition
description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

title: City of Forest Day Prospect Park South Street Tree Care
description: Volunteer with the NYC Parks Stewardship Team for City of Forest Day across New York City! Come work with NYC Parks Stewardship to care for local street trees! Volunteers will learn how to aerate, cultivate, mulch, and identify street trees. They will also learn about the important roles street trees play in New York City. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

title: City of Forest Day
description: Join us for the 5th annual City of Forest Day, when we will be planting climate adapted trees, shrubs, and herbaceous plugs to restore the understory near the Nature Center trail for years to come.  Presented by Forest for All NYC in partnership with the Parks and Open Space Partners coalition and NYC Department of Parks and Recreation (NYC Parks), City of Forest Day is an annual day of activities across the city to raise awareness of the importance of the New York City urban forest, and the essential role New Yorkers play every day in caring for the “lungs” of our city.Additional instructions:  Dress in long pants and sleeves and wear sturdy boots or sneakers suitable for standing on uneven terrain and digging in the soil.
location: Greenbelt Nature Center (in Blood Root Valley)
categories: Volunteer | City of Forest Day

title: BollyX
description: BollyX is a Bollywood inspired cardio dance fitness class inspired and is driven by the heart-pumping, energetic rhythms of cultural music from all parts of India. The class embodies dynamic choreography and easy-to-follow dance aerobics. Choreography and workout routines have been set so everyone can enjoy the class (modifications for individual steps can be provided in class). No dance experience or Bollywood familiarity is required - just come with comfortable shoes, water, and your smiles!
registration_description: Registration has begun and ends on 10/3/2026.
categories: Dance | Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Recreation Center Programming | Exercise Classes

title: City of Forest Day: Mini Rapid Site Assessment (RSA) at Forest Park
description: Join NYC Parks Conservation and Monitoring team and learn about the rapid site assessment protocol as part of City of Forest Day. This process was designed as part of our forest management framework to quickly assess the ecological health of a specific forest area. Participants will learn about this process, how NYC Parks uses it, and how plant identification is a key component of this process. Please bring water and a snack as well as your smartphone or camera. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long socks, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty.  Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone.  To sign up a group of 2 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.
registration_description: Registration is required on the NYC Parks Stewardship page.
categories: Nature | Volunteer | City of Forest Day

title: City of Forest Day: Brady's Pond Park Forest Restoration
description: Volunteer with the NYC Parks Stewardship Team for City of Forest Day across New York City! Join NYC Parks in Brady's Pond Park as we celebrate our love of NYC’s urban forest and help steward the land. Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been made possible with funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.
registration_description: Registration is required on the NYC Parks Stewardship page.
categories: Nature | Volunteer | City of Forest Day

title: City of Forest Day Fungi Walk at Pugsley Creek Park
description: For City of Forest Day, join NYC Parks staff on a hike around Pugsley Creek Park to explore the diversity of fall fungi. Volunteers will learn how to identify these organisms and learn how to make iNaturalist observations of any other signs of nature you find along the way. Please bring water and a snack as well as your smartphone or camera! We will stay on trails and the hike will not be strenuous, but we will be walking for about an hour, so please dress appropriately. If you do not know how to use iNaturalist, arrive 15 minutes early and we will show you how! To sign up a group of 5 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.
registration_description: Registration is required on the NYC Parks Stewardship page.
location: Stephens Ave & O'Brien Ave (in Pugsley Creek Park)
categories: Education | Nature | Tours | Volunteer | Waterfront | Hiking | Walking

title: Third United Lenape / Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance, the nonprofit that sustains Prospect Park in partnership with the city, Éenda-Lunaapeewáhkiing Collective, which brings together Lunáapeew/Lenape communities who have been displaced across Turtle Island (North America), and American Indian Community House, which promotes the well-being and visibility of the American Indian community, for the Third United Lenape/Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park.Vendors will be open starting at 10 am and the Grand Entry will kick off the celebrations at 11 am each day.Please note that eventbrite RSVP is encouraged but not required.The first Pow Wow held in Prospect Park since 1972, and the third ever Lenape Pow Wow in New York City, this free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to reunite and share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Join the weekend of family friendly fun, culture, art and learning with Indigenous dancers, drummers, and artisan craft and food vendors.Learn more about the Pow Wow here.The Pow Wow is part of the Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the Lefferts Historic House museum to explore the lives, resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family.To explore more Lenape heritage and culture, we encourage you to visit the Halumii Ktapihna: Lenape Legacies and Futures exhibit at the Museum of the City of New York, beginning September 25.

description: Join Journei Bimwala for this 1.5–2 hour hands-on creative workshop that invites participants to explore the beauty, versatility, and artistic potential of plants through wearable art. Using both fresh and dried botanical materials, participants will create 2–3 unique handmade accessories such as earrings, bracelets, rings, hair accessories, and other botanical adornments using natural plant fibers and wildcrafted materials. The workshop encourages participants to see plants beyond food and medicine by highlighting their role in fashion, self-expression, culture, and art.Throughout the session, participants will learn simple techniques for designing and assembling wearable pieces using leaves, flowers, vines, seeds, grasses, and other natural materials. The workshop is designed to foster creativity, imagination, and a deeper connection to the natural world while introducing participants to sustainable and plant-based crafting practices. Participants will also explore how adornment has historically been used across cultures as a form of identity, celebration, and artistic expression.The workshop will conclude with a celebratory mini photoshoot where participants will wear and showcase their handmade creations. These portraits will highlight the elegance and versatility of plant-based fashion while documenting each participant’s creativity and personal style. title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
location: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)

description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! title: Listening back to Parley
description: Join us for a discussion with exhibiting artists Angel Nevarez & Valerie Tevere and legendary hip-hop artist La Roka (Rokafella). Presented in conjunction with the exhibition As far as the ear can hear, this program revisits the artists' collaboration on Parley, one of four works in the exhibition that explores sound across the landscapes of the Bronx, New Orleans, and the Sonoran Desert. Originally commissioned for the 2015 exhibition When You Cut Into the Present, the Future Leaks Out at the Old Bronx Borough Courthouse, Parley, performed by pioneering Bronx b-girl Rokafella (Ana Garcia) and MC Lady L (Lynn Saunders) draws on the sampling techniques and lyrical traditions of early hip-hop to reanimate questions of truth, justice, and hope. Using the musical framework of call and response to form a multilingual dialogue between two voices, Parley reflects Nevarez & Tevere's ongoing interest in framing sound and listening as a transformative practice that connects fragmented histories and collective memory to open new forms of relation. Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. The Glyndor Terrace Garden is accessible via a bluestone path that begins south of the Glyndor House entrance and continues along its western perimeter towards an ADA-compliant ramp located at the Glyndor Terrace Garden’s north entrance.

title: Opening Reception: Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures by Billy Cleary
description: Van Cortlandt Park in PicturesPhotography by Billy Cleary Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3, 2026 | 3:00–5:00 PMVan Cortlandt House Museum presents Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures, a photography exhibition by Riverdale photographer Billy Cleary celebrating the landscapes, wildlife, and changing seasons of Van Cortlandt Park.A Riverdale resident for more than three decades, Cleary has spent years photographing the places and scenes that define his surroundings. His images capture familiar views of Van Cortlandt Park throughout the year, from tree-lined paths and expansive fields to the park’s ponds, wildlife, and historic entrances. Together, the photographs offer a personal portrait of one of the Bronx’s most significant green spaces through the eyes of a longtime neighbor.Cleary’s interest in photography took on new importance during the pandemic, when he began sharing more of his work on social media. Messages from people who were largely confined to their homes and looked forward to seeing his photographs encouraged him to continue documenting and sharing the landscapes around him. His work has since appeared in group exhibitions with the Riverdale Art Association and in solo exhibitions at the Riverdale-Yonkers Society for Ethical Culture and An Beal Bocht Café.The public is invited to meet the photographer and view the exhibition during an opening reception on Saturday, October 3, from 3:00 to 5:00 PM at Van Cortlandt House Museum. Light refreshments will be served.Please note: The opening reception is for guests ages 21 and over. IDs will be checked at the door.Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures will remain on view through November 8, 2026.Accessibility: at this time, the historic house is accessed using one set of stairs. The exhibition opening reception will take place on the first floor.
location: Van Cortlandt House Museum (in Van Cortlandt Park)

title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

title: Third United Lenape / Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow
description: Join Prospect Park Alliance, the nonprofit that sustains Prospect Park in partnership with the city, Éenda-Lunaapeewáhkiing Collective, which brings together Lunáapeew/Lenape communities who have been displaced across Turtle Island (North America), and American Indian Community House, which promotes the well-being and visibility of the American Indian community, for the Third United Lenape/Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park.Vendors will be open starting at 10 am and the Grand Entry will kick off the celebrations at 11 am each day.Please note that eventbrite RSVP is encouraged but not required.The first Pow Wow held in Prospect Park since 1972, and the third ever Lenape Pow Wow in New York City, this free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to reunite and share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Join the weekend of family friendly fun, culture, art and learning with Indigenous dancers, drummers, and artisan craft and food vendors.Learn more about the Pow Wow here.The Pow Wow is part of the Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the Lefferts Historic House museum to explore the lives, resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family.To explore more Lenape heritage and culture, we encourage you to visit the Halumii Ktapihna: Lenape Legacies and Futures exhibit at the Museum of the City of New York, beginning September 25.
location: Lefrak Center at Lakeside (in Prospect Park)

title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
location: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
categories: History | Tours | It's My Park | Seniors

title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

title: Meet the Artists: Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper
description: Join us for a Meet the Artist program with Van Lier Community Trust Fellows Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper. At 2PM, Brown will discuss his site-responsive installation, Hush Harbor, which transforms the Sunroom into a contemporary, antebellum hush harbor—a secret gathering place of refuge and worship for enslaved people--through sculpture, moving image, and sound. This project draws on themes of Black survival and faith, exploring ideas related to embodied belief and the relationship between spirit and land. At 3PM, Cooper will discuss his Sun Porch exhibition, SHOWPIECE, which takes up entomological study as a metaphor for the ways trans and gender-variant people are scrutinized and classified by society. Cooper transforms the Sun Porch into an insectarium full of sculptural bugs contextual to the grounds of Wave Hill, fabricated from the packaging of hormone replacement therapy and other trans ephemera. This afternoon program includes conversations with the exhibiting artists and the activation of works on display.  Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. As part of the Sunroom Project Space, this program is designed collaboratively with the artists and takes various forms. Meet the Artist offers visitors, the artist's community, and others an opportunity to gain insight into the artist's creative process and the themes present in their work. Registration encouraged but not required, online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.

title: Works in Public Opening: 145th Street
description: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park at 145th Street, celebrating sculptures by Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson.Lindsey Francis Jones, City in Shapes, City in FishCity in Shapes, City in Fish invites viewers into the artist’s visual language through a cityscape of abstract shapes and color. Inspired by the craft and community of printmaking, the work incorporates images of six fish etched onto selected plexiglass, contributed by fellow printmakers and artists: Laurissa Widrick, Felix Bladbjerg, Kait Waldman, Stan Overstreet, Barbara Ganmen, and Scarlett Patino.Clare Burson, Unearthed.UNEARTHED is an installation of three steel forms inspired by the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos. It asks us to consider the inevitable and unexpected ways that history imposes itself on the present. When experienced with its accompanying soundscape, UNEARTHED also reminds us that our shared public spaces are nexus points for an infinite number of narratives that connect individuals and communities across time, those who lived here before us and those who will come after us.

categories: Art | Talks

title: Works in Public Opening: Riverside Park South
description: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park South, celebrating sculptures by Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca.About the Artists & ArtAlicia Ehni, Balancing A Peruvian shaman once told Ehni to carry a lemon in her purse, that it brings great harmony in life and in interactions with others. Two fractured pre-Columbian ceramics carry ancient coastal knowledge, opening possibilities to imagine a different future. Balancing reflects on the fragile relationships between people, nature, and the built environment.Robert Franca, The ChairsThe Chairs explores family as the foundation through which we understand ourselves and the world. Seen through a child’s perspective, the chairs embody imagination, openness, and freedom from conventional rules. Their human-like forms suggest movement and the ability to change. Ultimately, the chairs speak to the importance of finding balance — within ourselves, within families, and in navigating the challenges and uncertainties of an ever-changing world.

description: Fit & Lit is your ultimate dance cardio class, where high-energy movement meets heart-pumping music for a workout experience like no other! title: Garden Conflict Transformation Circle— A 2-Month Journey for Community Gardeners | Session #1
description: Even the most harmonious garden groups experience conflict—it's as natural as weeds sprouting between the tomatoes. But what if those challenging moments could become opportunities for deeper connection and stronger communities? Join mediators Skye Roper-Moses and Michelle Jackson for an intimate, two-month learning cohort designed specifically for community gardeners who are ready to transform the way they navigate conflict.Session 1: Conflict Transformation CircleShare real-life challenges in a confidential, supportive space with fellow gardeners. Together, you’ll co-create solutions and learn practical skills you can take directly back to your garden.Session 2: Conflict Transformation Experiential LabDeepen your practice through hands-on exercises. Learn how to address tensions before they take root and gain confidence facilitating difficult conversations. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
categories: Workshops | Virtual/Online Events | Gardening

title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen
categories: Education | Nature | Art

title: Wetland Wednesdays: Phragmites Control and Native Planting at Van Cortlandt Park
description: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland restoration along Van Cortlandt Lake. We cut back invasive phragmites (common reed) that crowds out native wetland plants and, as plants arrive, plant native willows and shrubs at the restoration sites.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from October 7th - October 28th. Dates are 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, and 10/28.Meeting Details:Location: Van Cortlandt Golf House. Meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms.Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.What to Bring:Long sleeves, long pants and boots (phragmites stems are sharp and the ground is wet)Water and a snackTools, gloves and training provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.
registration_description: Free. Please sign up for the specific date on Bloomerang Volunteer.
location: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
categories: Nature | Volunteer | It's My Park | Waterfront

title: Team RIVER Volunteers
description: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

title: Volunteer Workday: Howard Garden
description: Join Howard Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for an engaging volunteer day to prepare the garden for new raised beds! Volunteers can get involved with weeding, dismantling old raised beds, and leveling soil. We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks.Join us for the whole project!Day 1 (Wed. Oct. 7) – Garden Site PrepDay 2 (Sat. Oct. 10) – New Bed BuildingDay 3 (Wed. Oct. 21) – Filling Beds & PlantingHoward Garden was founded in the late 1980's by community activists and artists who've made a lasting impact in the Brownsville community. These gardeners are still active to this day, and are excited to pass along the knowledge and skills gained through decades of environmental stewardship. This is a great opportunity for beginner and seasoned volunteers looking to join a growing garden!Register here!For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

title: Gardening with Ground Covers
description: Have you ever wanted an alternative to woodchips or landscape fabric? If so, this is a workshop for you. Ground covers are an excellent way to protect exposed soils while also providing habitat and improving soil stability. In this workshop we will explore a variety of garden situations, plants and expand the definition of “ground covers.” Participants will learn how to select, establish and design with ground covers. No matter the size of your garden, ground covers are a great step towards building a sustainable and more resilient community garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

title: Author Talk with David Rocco: Fireboats of the FDNY
description: For the last century and a half, FDNY fireboats have played a vital role in protecting New York City’s waterfront. On Thursday, October 8, the Bayside Historical Society welcomes author and photographer David Rocco for an illustrated presentation exploring the history and evolution of these remarkable vessels.With more than 500 miles of shoreline, New York City has long relied on specialized fireboats to respond to fires along the waterfront and aboard ships. Using historic photographs and images, Rocco will trace their development from the early wooden-hull tugboats to the highly specialized vessels that serve the city today.Rocco has been involved in numerous historic preservation and cultural projects throughout the Hudson Valley and New York City. In 2023, he prepared the successful nomination that placed the retired FDNY fireboat John D. McKean on both the State and National Registers of Historic Places. He currently serves as Vice President of the Fireboat McKean Preservation Project.The presentation will be followed by a question-and-answer session and book signing.Admission is $10 for BHS members and $15 for non-members. Purchase tickets on the BHS website: https://www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/author-talk-with-david-rocco-fireboats-of-the-fdny.This event is part of Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.

title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.
categories: Education | Art | History

title: Proximity Exhibition
description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.
location: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)

title: General Interest Meeting
description: Join Farmer Yon, our volunteers, and GreenThumb Community Engagement Coordinators Gregory Anderson and Rain Abdalla for an evening of collective visioning. The Hattie Carthan Herban Farm has undergone 8 community powered volunteer clean up days, where we learned about the history of the garden and the herbs growing there. Now, we must find ways to connect with this history while determining what the future holds. We seek to answer questions like:What does becoming a member of this garden mean?What are the roles and responsibilities of a member? How does the garden serve us and the public?Come ready to sip on herbal tea, journal and share your ideas - BYOT (bring your own tea!) If you've volunteered before and would like to brew something from the garden, please reach out to Rain.Abdalla@parks.nyc.gov ahead of time.RSVP here (bit.ly/HerbanFarmFriday)

title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

title: NYRR Open Run: Inwood Hill Park
description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration Run
description: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage with Open Run! Wear your home country’s colors!  NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.
categories: Hispanic Heritage Month | Running/Jogging

title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
location: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
categories: History | Tours | It's My Park | Seniors

title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

title: Proximity Exhibition
description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. title: "The Light That Shines Through the Universe": Lectures and Meditations - Monuments to War
description: As part of the public programming for Tuan Andrew Nguyen’s High Line Plinth commission, The Light That Shines Through the Universe, the High Line presents a monthly lecture and guided meditation series at the Spur. Presented in partnership with the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, the series invites visitors to engage more deeply with themes central to Nguyen’s work. Each session features a lecture by a scholar, artist, or cultural leader, followed by a guided meditation led by an invited practitioner.The series is hosted by Tashi Chödrön, Himalayan Programs and Communities Ambassador at the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, who, in her two decades with the Rubin, has led meditation programs for over ten years and is the current host of the Rubin’s Mindfulness Meditation podcast. Through this combination of intellectual and contemplative practice, the series invites audiences to pause, reflect, and consider the artwork’s historical and philosophical themes through both thought and experience.Closing the series, Nico Rodriguez, deputy director of Monuments Lab, considers Nguyen’s work alongside contemporary artistic approaches to memorialization. The discussion explores how artists reimagine monuments to war by transforming sites of violence into spaces for remembrance, reflection, and collective healing.The lecture will be followed by a guided meditation by Steve Clorfeine, a meditation teacher from the Shambhala tradition with over 40 years of experience.Rain date: October 11, 2 – 3pm

title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
location: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
categories: History | Tours | It's My Park | Seniors

description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. title: Saunksquas, Sassafras, and Moccasins: Walking Tour with Oleana Whispering Dove
description: Join Oleana Whispering Dove for a walking tour on the Wave Hill Grounds, highlighting the rich legacy of the region’s Indigenous Saunksquas and the profound impact of these women throughout history.  This tour reflects on historical imprint of known figures like Sojourner Truth, Maya Angelou, Condoleezza Rice,  Susan B. Anthony, Matilda Cage, Lucretia Mott, and Gloria Steinem with earlier unsung female leaders known as Saunk Squa’s; Mama Nuchwe, Dostou, Wastawancett, Lyssie, Annetie Pownock. These Native American women held the highest-ranking leadership roles in their communities and were honored by European settlers with titles like Her Royal Majesty, The King’s Queen, and Indian Princess—recognizing their powerful status and influence as they played a pivotal role in governing their regional tribes, leading land negotiations, and signing land treaties. Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.

title: Hart Island Tour (North Island)
description: Hart Island is the largest public cemetery in the country and has served New York City since 1869. While Hart Island is currently only used for city burials, the island is deeply connected to New York City institutions. It has served many uses since the 19th Century, including a military training ground, a quarantine station, a psychiatric hospital, a reform school, a rehabilitation facility, a missile base, and a jail.Join the Urban Park Rangers to explore Hart Island's unique past, present, and future. Participants are chosen by lottery. Lottery registration opens on Wednesday September 30, 2026 and ends Thursday October 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.  Please Note:-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Anyone who was not registered will not be permitted to attend.-  If you are selected for the program, you will receive a series of emails confirming your selection and must respond as soon as possible to avoid forfeiting your spot. - Hart Island is only accessible via ferry. Selected participants will be provided details regarding program arrival and other specifics.- There are no indoor facilities, restrooms or drinking fountains on Hart Island. There are portable restrooms on the island.- This tour covers historical context of Hart Island and is about two hours of walking, some parts on uneven terrain. Please dress appropriately for the weather and the terrain.- Program may be cancelled due to inclement weather at the discretion of ferry operations.
categories: History | Urban Park Rangers

title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

title: Wetland Wednesdays: Phragmites Control and Native Planting at Van Cortlandt Park
description: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland restoration along Van Cortlandt Lake. We cut back invasive phragmites (common reed) that crowds out native wetland plants and, as plants arrive, plant native willows and shrubs at the restoration sites.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from October 7th - October 28th. Dates are 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, and 10/28.Meeting Details:Location: Van Cortlandt Golf House. Meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms.Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.What to Bring:Long sleeves, long pants and boots (phragmites stems are sharp and the ground is wet)Water and a snackTools, gloves and training provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.
registration_description: Free. Please sign up for the specific date on Bloomerang Volunteer.
location: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
categories: Nature | Volunteer | It's My Park | Waterfront

title: Team RIVER Volunteers
description: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

title: Midtown Music in Greeley Square Park
description: Featuring a multitude of musical moods ranging from pop-up performances for passers-by to festival shows curated by cultural partners, Midtown Music has something for every ear. Hear NYC’s finest singer-songwriters workshop their newest material, catch up-and-coming Indie or Americana acts, relax to some jazz or party with a brass band.  Check out our website for additional Friday and Saturday shows!
categories: Free Summer Concerts

title: Kids in Motion: Hunts Point Playground
description: The Kids in Motion Program engages children in active, outdoor play. A NYC Parks staff member leads four to seven hours of free activities in NYC's playgrounds, including organized sports. games, fitness, demos, board games, water games, and more!Kids in Motion is a free, drop-in program without registration. Children can head to the playground during the listed hours of operation to participate. Occasionally a Kids in motion program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions. Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. Kids in Motion is not a childcare program and NYC Parks is not responsible for the well-being of attendees.
categories: Arts & Crafts | Games | Best for Kids | Sports
